Miyake, et al., Science, 330, 1234 (2010) (DOI 10.1126/science.1195996). While Reference 8 (a 2010 PERC conference proceedings paper on the same initial study) is co-cited once in the Introduction ([7,8]), Reference 7 is the primary published journal article and is the work specifically cited as Study 1 throughout the Study Design and Results sections (note that the blind coding's evidence_quote failed literal verification only because it reconstructed text across the two-column layout).

decisions.quote:
In this prior study, we found that the gender gap on
   exams and the FMCE among students who completed two 15-minute self-affirmation writing exercises was significantly
   reduced compared to the gender gap among students who completed neutral writing exercises. In a follow-up study we
   replicated the self-affirmation intervention in a later semester of the same course, with the same instructor. In this paper,
   we report the details and preliminary results of the replication study, where we find similar patterns along exams and
   course grades, but do not observe these patterns along the FMCE.
decisions.reason: The authors explicitly present the replication outcome for Miyake et al. (2010) as partly supporting and partly not ('Successes and Challenges'): they find similar patterns and significant positive effects of self-affirmation for female students on exam scores and course grades, but explicitly contrast the Force and Motion Concept Evaluation (FMCE) post-test results, stating that the patterns from Study 1 were not replicated on the FMCE. Both shipped and blind codings agree on 'mixed'.
